answers.a_personRegistryAndWhatIsPerson: Functionally yes, but very thin. pom.xml:14 'Service to manage AlgoTrade Platform Persons'. PersonEntity carries ONLY demographic identity - id, a server-minted uuid, firstName, lastName, email, birthday + a userId pointer (PersonEntity.java:12-20). No trading or customer-lifecycle state at all (no account, balance, entitlement, tariff, KYC, address, document) and no relation to account-service. So Person = the people/customer profile record belonging to a platform user, nothing more. The author treats person and user as near-synonyms: 'exception.person.not.found' renders in Russian as 'the USER is not registered' (exception_message_rus.properties:2) and the duplicate constant is ERROR_USER_ALREADY_REGISTERED (GlobalErrorCode.java:8).
answers.b_outboundCallsAndClientType: NONE - zero outbound calls. 0 occurrences of RestTemplate, WebClient, FeignClient, @EnableFeignClients, ExchangeStrategies or HttpClient in the Java sources; the module's only 'WebClient' text is System.Net.WebClient in the Maven wrapper script mvnw.cmd:145, not application code. The pom confirms intent: no spring-cloud-starter-openfeign and no spring-boot-starter-webflux, so WebClient could not even compile. Consequence: PersonRequest.userId is persisted unverified (PersonServiceImpl.java:19-23). person-service is a pure callee. For orientation only, cited from the sibling ARTIFACT .opencode/project/analysis/user-service.json (sibling source not read): the platform's inter-service client IS RestTemplate, and user-service is the caller - GET http://localhost:3535/persons/{personId} (UserController.java:25,104).
answers.c_consulRegistrationAndRandomPort: Annotation-free auto-registration: spring-cloud-starter-consul-discovery on the classpath (pom.xml:44-47) + the bootstrap context re-enabled (pom.xml:23-31, bootstrap.yml) -> Spring Cloud Consul auto-registers the app under service id 'person-service' (spring.application.name, bootstrap.yml:2) at spring.cloud.consul.host localhost:8500 with instance-id '${spring.cloud.client.hostname}_${spring.application.name}:${random.value}' and register-health-check: false (config-service person-service.yml:35-42). No @EnableDiscoveryClient is needed on Boot 2.x and none exists. server.port: 0 (person-service.yml:1-2) lets the OS assign an ephemeral port every boot; the fixed address is replaced by Consul name resolution at the gateway, and ${random.value} in the instance-id is what lets several instances share a host without registry collisions. Consequences: Dockerfile EXPOSE 8080 is meaningless, and no document, script or test may hardcode a person-service port.
answers.d_consumerAndDataDuplication: Nothing inside person-service consumes or replicates user-service data - no client, listener, cache or sync, and no inbound integration point beyond the 4 handlers. Provable in scope: {firstName,lastName,email,birthday,userId} is repeated verbatim 3x (PersonEntity.java:16-20, PersonRequest.java:9-13, PersonResponse.java:9-14) while the entity stores its OWN email and also points at another aggregate via userId. POSSIBLE DATA-DUPLICATION FINDING, corroborated by the pre-existing artifact .opencode/project/analysis/user-service.json (sibling source NOT read): user-service holds UserEntity.personId as a plain column AND hand-maintains controller/dto/PersonDto.java mirroring (id, uuid, firstName, lastName, email, birthday) embedded in UserResponse.person - the demographic block is therefore stored twice platform-wide, person-service the write side, user-service an unversioned hand-copied read model. Two drifts visible from this side: (i) PersonResponse does NOT expose uuid (PersonResponse.java:9-14) though the sibling mirror is recorded as containing it, and Jackson NON_NULL (person-service.yml:32-33) omits it; (ii) PersonResponse DOES expose userId, which the mirror is not recorded as having. The reference direction is also inverted (person.userId vs user.personId) - a circular pair of unconstrained id columns.
answers.e_followUp: Phase 6 question: is uuid the external identifier? It is minted (PersonServiceImpl.java:20), mapped away (PersonMapper.java:16), never unique-constrained, never queried - while a sibling is documented as expecting exactly that field.

recommendations: Add spring-boot-starter-validation and constrain PersonRequest (@NotBlank firstName/lastName, @Email email, @NotNull birthday) with @Valid at PersonController.java:22,:39 - arbitrary input, including an unverified userId, is persisted today.

Unify the error contract: PersonGlobalExceptionHandler.java:34-39 returns a bare string for unexpected errors while typed errors return ErrorResponse{code,message}, and both answer 400. Use ErrorResponse everywhere; 404 for ERROR_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND.
Adopt Flyway/Liquibase before t_persons holds real customer data - ddl-auto: update (person-service.yml:29) cannot express the unique constraints uuid/email need and there is no schema history.
Settle the person/user boundary: stop persisting the same demographic block in two services, resolve the circular personId <-> userId pair, decide whether userId must be validated.
Decide the uuid contract - expose it + unique constraint + lookup endpoint, or delete it; today it is written, hidden and unused while a sibling expects it.
Delete or wire up PersonAlreadyRegisteredException / ERROR_USER_ALREADY_REGISTERED (1001) - dead code implying an unimplemented duplicate-email rule.
Remove <source>10</source><target>10</target> (person-service/pom.xml:100-101) so the module inherits java.version 17 (pom.xml:31) like the openjdk:17 image.
Add @Transactional (or one bulk update) to PersonServiceImpl.update/delete - each is currently two transactions.
Stop logging whole person DTOs at INFO (PersonController.java:23,34,43) - PII lands in logs/person-service.log.

Rotate and externalise the datasource credentials (person-service.yml:46-47, by property name) and narrow management.endpoints.web.exposure.include (person-service.yml:18) - /env echoes them. Set register-health-check: true so Consul can evict a dead instance.
Add the module's first tests - @WebMvcTest of PersonController, @DataJpaTest of PersonRepository: 4 endpoints, 1 repository, 0 tests, so all verification today is manual and runtime-only.
